Construction applications connect drawings and models to materials, sequence, code-aware decision making, and safe work. Small fabricated aids are useful for learning layout or communication; they do not replace approved structural components, code requirements, or qualified review.

## Project directions

:::: {.ter-project-grid}
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Layout and hole-spacing template
<p class="ter-course-code">TCJ2O · Gauge family</p>
Create a template for one repeatable layout task such as shelf-pin spacing, hardware centres, or model framing positions.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Measure hardware → choose datum → exact drawing → test cut → field simulation</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Centre-to-centre dimensions, marking, cumulative error, annotations</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Introductory–intermediate · under 300 mm long</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Hardboard or plywood that remains flat</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Reinforce narrow bridges and provide a clear reference edge</dd><dt>Safety</dt><dd>Use as a marking guide only; clamp work and follow tool procedures</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=construction&type=jigs-gauges">Construction templates</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../03-laser-cutting/03-measure-place.qmd">Measure + Place</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Test accumulated error over five repeated placements</dd></dl>
:::
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Joinery teaching model
<p class="ter-course-code">TCJ2O / senior TCJ · Display family</p>
Build an enlarged, removable model that explains how one joint transfers load and where it may fail.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Joint research → section sketch → scaled parts → assembly → load-path annotation</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Orthographic thinking, scale, joinery vocabulary, communication</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Intermediate · 250–400 mm demonstration model</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Plywood, dimensional offcuts, or printed connectors</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Teaching model only; distinguish model behaviour from building performance</dd><dt>Safety</dt><dd>No claim of code compliance or structural rating</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=construction&type=project-components">Joint and stand starters</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../03-laser-cutting/05-assemblies-hybrid-fabrication.qmd">Assemblies + Hybrid Fabrication</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Compare the same connection in wood, steel, and masonry systems</dd></dl>
:::
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Portable layout-tool module
<p class="ter-course-code">Senior TCJ · Portable work module</p>
Organize a defined set of layout tools for quick transport, inventory, and use at a mock work station.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Workflow observation → inventory → centre-of-mass study → prototype → carry test</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Tool access, handles, retention, fasteners, material efficiency</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Intermediate · one-person carry, instructor-set mass limit</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Plywood shell with replaceable dividers and standard hardware</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Load-test handle and joints; retain tools during transport</dd><dt>Safety</dt><dd>Exclude sharp or heavy tools until retention is reviewed</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=construction&type=french-cleat">Modular organization parts</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../03-laser-cutting/07-wall-bench-module.qmd">Wall + Bench Module</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Adapt the module to dock safely at a fixed bench</dd></dl>
:::
::::

**Curriculum context:** Use the project to support drawing interpretation, measurement, materials, construction systems, sequencing, safe tool use, environmental choices, and careers in the current TCJ course.
